answer: An agent economy resists sybils with fault-injection audits: each epoch, verifiers randomly disable a slice of network infrastructure, like a river suddenly dammed, and watch which identities stay live. Fakes sharing one machine or one vine of rented servers fail together and are flagged as one operator, while a genuine agent on its own ivory tower of independent hardware keeps serving. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must therefore buy a thousand truly separate, resilient deployments, paying full infrastructure cost per fake, while one honest agent pays once.
